device.description: quad 16-bit voltage-output DAC with 24-bit serial interface, quick load, daisy-chain SDO, double-buffered inputs (LOAD, LDAC) and reset to zero or mid scale
device.note: dac7634.pdf (SBAS134B) p.3-4 (electrical characteristics: VDD digital 4.75-5.25 V, VIH 0.7 VDD), p.5 (pin descriptions), p.6 (pin configuration), p.22 (digital interface, serial data input, Table 1 truth table), p.23 (Table 2 shift register, serial-data output, coding), p.24 (Figures 61-64), p.25 (Table 3 timing)

registers.name: INA
registers.note: DAC A input register (A1 A0 = 00); loaded from the shift register while LOAD is low (Table 1); power-on code not stated (reset 0)

registers.name: INB
registers.note: DAC B input register (A1 A0 = 01); loaded from the shift register while LOAD is low (Table 1); power-on code not stated (reset 0)

registers.name: INC
registers.note: DAC C input register (A1 A0 = 10); loaded from the shift register while LOAD is low (Table 1); power-on code not stated (reset 0)

registers.name: IND
registers.note: DAC D input register (A1 A0 = 11); loaded from the shift register while LOAD is low (Table 1); power-on code not stated (reset 0)

registers.name: DACA
registers.note: DAC A DAC register; all four loaded from the input registers on the LDAC rising edge (Table 1)

registers.name: DACB
registers.note: DAC B DAC register; all four loaded from the input registers on the LDAC rising edge (Table 1)

registers.name: DACC
registers.note: DAC C DAC register; all four loaded from the input registers on the LDAC rising edge (Table 1)

registers.name: DACD
registers.note: DAC D DAC register; all four loaded from the input registers on the LDAC rising edge (Table 1)

registers.name: SR
registers.note: internal: the 24-bit serial shift register (A1 A0 QUICK LOAD, five unused bits, D15-D0), shifted out on SDO

commands.name: Write
commands.note: 24-bit word A1 A0 QUICK-LOAD X X X X X D15-D0, MSB first, clocked on CLK rising (p.22). Quick load 1: the code goes to all four input registers; 0: to the one A1 A0 select (channelMap on the 3-bit A1 A0 QL capture). The shift register goes to the input register(s) while LOAD is low; modeled as written when CS rises. The last 24 bits before CS rises are decoded

protocol.note: SDO is the shift register's output (driven, p.23); CS and CLK are ORed, CS should rise only while CLK is high (p.22), hence mode 3

ldac.note: DAC register load, rising-edge triggered: all DAC registers (p.5, Table 1)

clear.note: rising-edge triggered: loads zero (RSTSEL low) or mid scale 8000h (RSTSEL high)

pages: p.3-4 (electrical characteristics: VDD digital 4.75-5.25 V, VIH 0.7 VDD), p.5 (pin descriptions), p.6 (pin configuration), p.22 (digital interface, serial data input, Table 1 truth table), p.23 (Table 2 shift register, serial-data output, coding), p.24 (Figures 61-64), p.25 (Table 3 timing)
notModeled: analog: outputs, force/sense pins, differential reference inputs, single/dual supply operation, current-source configuration, settling

LOAD: the shift register is copied into the addressed (or, with quick load, every) input register while LOAD is low; the schema has no load-strobe pin, so the word is written when CS rises (a frame without a LOAD pulse still updates the input register in the model)
RST does not change the serial shift register in the chip (the model's clear leaves SR as well)
power-on state of the registers is not stated in the datasheet (reset 0)
daisy chain: SDO shifts the previous 24-bit word, then the real part passes the incoming bits through; the model shifts the previous word then zeros, so chained devices do not receive data
CS and CLK are interchangeable (ORed); with CS tied low the shift register runs on CLK alone (Table 1 note); a CS rising edge while CLK is low shifts one extra bit
timing limits of Table 3 (no SDO propagation delay is given)
variants: DAC7634E / EB are linearity grades of the same chip. DAC7654 (dac7654.pdf) uses the same 24-bit word in an LQFP-64 with IOVDD and an internal reference.
